newsitem.title: UK: Man killed in N.Ireland shooting - police.
newsitem.headline: Man killed in N.Ireland shooting - police.

text.p: A man was killed in a gun attack near an Irish nationalist stronghold in west Belfast on Friday night, police said.
"A man has been shot dead," a police spokesman said.
The Royal Ulster Constabulary was unable to say whether the shooting was linked to Northern Ireland's long-running sectarian conflict between rival guerrilla groups.
However a spokesman for Sinn Fein, the political arm of the Irish Republican Army, said the victim was a Catholic and blamed pro-British Protestant guerrillas for his death.

"All the indications are at this stage that this was an attack by a (Protestant) Loyalist death sqaud. It is additional evidence that confirms that the Loyalist cessation of violence ended some time ago," he said. The shooting comes during a time of heightened tension and a deteriorating security climate in the British province, where rival factions are in conflict over the future of British rule.
A ceasefire called by guerrillas who are loyal to Britain has been in operation since October 1994 but has grown increasingly unstable as a result of a surge in IRA hostilities since December.
The IRA, which is fighting to end British rule and merge Northern Ireland with largely Catholic Ireland, ended a 17-month truce in February 1996.
Initial details of Friday night's shooting were sketchy but police said the attack happened in a housing development at Broadway, near the city's Catholic Falls Road.
Neighbours said the victim was a quiet family man with several children.
"The man has been confirmed as a fatality," said a security source. " Someone has approached him and he has been shot. He would appear to have been singled out."
The killing follows a renewed spate of guerrilla violence.
The IRA has killed two British soldiers in the province since last October and launched a string of mortar and grenade attacks on police and soldiers.
A policeman and soldier were seriously wounded late on Thursday when a bomb was detonated beside a security force patrol in a Catholic enclave in east Belfast.

Britain blamed the IRA. Loyalists were blamed for a failed bomb attack on Sinn Fein offices in Monaghan town in the republic of Ireland two weeks ago. That was the fourth attack since December to be attributed by security sources to Protestant hardliners determined to retaliate for IRA actions.

Loyalist extremists were also suspected of the murder of a Catholic taxi driver in Portadown town last July, during sectarian tension that swept the province in an annual period of Protestant parades.
The Combined Loyalist Military Command has insisted, however, that the ceasefire remains in place.
